soundness_flags.one_line: The cited DDK theorem uses an upper covariance norm and lasso-specific quantities, not the stated two-sided uniform covariance-eigenvalue condition; replace the citation or retag and justify the compact covariance class.

soundness_flags.one_line: VarandoHansen2020 states the Lyapunov model but does not support trace-one common-time normalization as a named standard condition; cite a source for scale invariance or describe it as this proposal's normalization.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The proceedings article studies unknown-diffusion continuous-time stationary systems and defines identifiability of the sign of a given drift entry across compatible observational covariances.

source_verification_receipts.version: SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications 44(4), 2023
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The journal version states that the drift is globally identifiable exactly when the graph is simple under diagonal volatility, and gives the skew-symmetric Lyapunov-fiber parametrization.

The cited theorem defines cΣ as the upper operator norm of Σ and gives an irrepresentability-plus-sample-size lasso result with a beta-min threshold; it does not state a uniform lower covariance-eigenvalue bound.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 1, equation (2) and surrounding model description

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 95-97, abstract and introduction; pp. 107-111, Proposition 3.3
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article gives a trek-rule representation, with an acyclic polynomial specialization and a marginal-variance lower bound for a restricted acyclic sign regime.
The paper constructs identified-set estimators and confidence regions by inversion of a sample criterion and develops consistency, rates, and inference.
The article studies inference for directionally differentiable transforms and explicitly uses tangent cones in its asymptotic analysis.

The paper defines weak regularity through local degree-zero homogeneity, proves impossibility of consistent or equivariant estimation in that setting, and characterizes an underlying regular parameter.
The preprint uses higher-order cumulant equations under non-Gaussianity to obtain generic full-drift identifiability and derives an estimator's asymptotic distribution.
The preprint characterizes model equivalence for acyclic graphical continuous Lyapunov models with uncorrelated noise.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the two unsupported standard-tag citations: cite a source actually imposing compact two-sided covariance eigenvalue bounds, and either cite a scale-invariance source for trace normalization or label trace-one as a proposal-specific gauge.

State an explicit finite decision algorithm for the four-sector certificate, including its input representation, face enumeration count, rank-degenerate handling, and termination bound; this turns the certificate from an exact low-dimensional characterization into a constructive identification result.

Lift the product-polarity result beyond one hand-fixed two-cycle by proving a transfer theorem for a generic class of feedback subgraphs or a strict extension over two named graph-level sign comparators.
